findings.statement: The F-BAR-11 byte gate and the decision path key on DIFFERENT things, so they can disagree: the byte entry refuses by the PATH-OWNING root (`_owning_root(path, roots)`), while the decision path admits a candidate by the LOCATION's `root_id`. With nested roots a handle the decision path can elect is refused `policy_denied`.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:1775 `and str(item.get("root_id") or "") in reusable_root_ids` (list built at resolver.py:1348-1350) vs resolver.py:2093-2097 `owning_root = _owning_root(path, roots)` + `owning_root.root_id not in reusable_root_ids`. Probe (temp dir; outer root reusable, nested `inner` root `reusable_for_filing=False`, one real filing): the scan writes BOTH `('inner','2025.pdf')` and `('outer','inner/deep/2025.pdf')`; `_owning_root(target, roots).root_id == 'inner'`; `reusable_root_ids == ['outer']`, so the outer location passes the decision gate while the byte gate computes a denied owner. `_owning_root` also ranks by `len(str(root.path))` on the CONFIGURED path while containment is decided on `os.path.realpath` (resolver.py:378-381 vs :396-409), so 'longest match' is not a real-path longest match. The fix's own comment claims the opposite: resolver.py:2088-2091 'so the three can never disagree'; test docstring test_r4bar11:12-13.
findings.why_it_matters: It is a false refusal on the read path: a caller that asks for bytes of a handle the resolver just elected gets not_found/policy_denied. The current production config has four disjoint roots (companies / dayu portfolio / Dropbox / future_lake), so there is no live impact today; the defect appears as soon as two roots nest (the config comment invites future roots) or when a location's real path falls inside a more specific root via a link.

findings.statement: A root that declares a REGISTERED adapter for which the scanner has no implementation now fails the ENTIRE catalog scan even when the activation flag is off, where the legacy walk used to serve it. The declaration is accepted by the config loader, so a config-only 'future root' can brick every root's scan.
findings.evidence: scanner.py:855 + :863 feed the adapter path; scan_root_strategy converts any dispatch failure into `ScannerFacadeError` (scanner.py:1921-1932) which propagates out of `_scan_catalog_impl` (scan_catalog re-raises after _interrupt_scan_run, scanner.py:1896-1898). Probe (temp dir, two roots: adapter-free `good` + `generic_root` with adapter_id='generic_document_v1', `scan_catalog(config, store, v2_scan_shadow=False)`): PRE-FIX dispatch `scan_root_strategy(gen_root, (), v2_scan_shadow=False)` -> OK, 1 candidate; POST-FIX whole scan -> `ScannerFacadeError: v2 scanner unavailable (fail closed): root 'generic_root' adapter 'generic_document_v1' has no scanner adapter implementation`, and `SELECT ... FROM locations` is EMPTY -- the healthy root was indexed by nothing. The adapter is registered (adapters/registry.py:42-47) but has no scanner factory (adapter_dispatch.py:29-33); config load only requires registration (config.py:127-131).
findings.why_it_matters: The change's stated boundary ('only how adapter-declared roots are scanned') hides a whole-scan failure mode: one bad root starves the other three production roots -- the same shape this very batch treats as a defect at document level (F-B10R2 'one bad row starves the queue'). Mitigating context: for flag-ON scans this fail-closed already existed, and the production snapshot has `v2_scan_shadow: true` (evidence/a05-readonly-manifest-run-A06-2-stdout.txt), so the current production behaviour is unchanged; what is new is that flag-off / no-snapshot scans can now abort this way.
